source.display_title: 05/31/2026 - Hiten Patel x Andrew Musial  — Follow Up

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter referenced anywhere in the transcript.

prospect.name: Hiten Patel
prospect.location: Atlanta, Georgia, USA (Eastern time); moving to New Jersey in August or September 2026
prospect.occupation: Dentist, recently qualified — 'I'm still freshly out of school'. Works 7-9 hours a day hunched over patients, with roughly an hour's commute each way.
prospect.training_background: Formerly very fit and highly mobile through kettlebell training; owns a full home set from 5 to 35 lb and wants heavier. Now goes to the gym most days or every other day but describes it as going through the motions — treadmill, some weights, sauna. Ran a 7 to 7.5 minute mile a year ago, now 10 to 11 minutes. Plays soccer and used to road cycle; has not cycled in eight months or more. Previously followed a trainer's PDF programme, which he stopped. Sleeps 7-8 hours, tracks with a WHOOP, sleep score usually 75-90. Eats out roughly twice a day.
prospect.medical: Two herniated discs at L4, L5 and S1 sustained in 2017-18, treated with physical therapy rather than surgery. Now largely settled but with lower back tightness when he sits too long and intermittent sciatica flare-ups — 'sometimes I get a flare-up of sciatica, but for the most part, it's just sensitive soreness here and there' — and it flares from being hunched over at work. Digestive problems and constipation for the past seven to eight months, now on medication. Went through a period of depression after moving to Atlanta; currently in therapy and on medication — 'I started therapy and medications to fix my digestive issues and feel a lot better'. Occasional alcohol and cannabis use described in the context of comfort-seeking.

signals: Explicitly wants a former self back: 'I'm one of those persons that used to be super fit ... I got really good shape. And then I'm just, over time, you kind of just like get out of it. And then now I want to get back into it.'
A datable hard season — a move to a new city in August, a new job, digestive illness and a depressive episode all at once
Carries the regret openly: 'I was like, dude, I have so much belly fat. Like what is going on? ... what the hell is going on? What are you doing?'
Measures the loss precisely against his old self, from a 7-minute mile to an 11-minute mile
Not the prehab fighter: he describes the acute phase as behind him — 'I don't feel that anymore ... I feel a little more clear headed'

goals.text: Move properly again — play soccer without being wrecked for days and get back on the road bike
Get to 155-160 lb and roughly 12-15% body fat, revised down on the call from 'super shredded' at 10-12%
Recover the mobility he had when kettlebells were the centre of his training
Feel confident again — 'my confidence comes down to how I'm able to move my body and how I feel on a day-to-day'
Have the physical durability to open a large cosmetic dental practice — 'dentistry is hard on your body ... if I'm not fit, it hurts my body, and I can't do good dentistry'
Keep his lower back stable enough to work hunched over without flare-ups
Stop seeking comfort in food and be outgoing again rather than defaulting to the couch

pains.text: Trains almost daily with no plan — 'I'm physically in the gym, but my mind is probably somewhere else'; some days it is just a treadmill warm-up and the sauna
Eight months to a year of decline since moving to Atlanta; mile pace has gone from 7 minutes to 10 or 11
A depressive episode with food used as comfort, now in therapy and on medication
Digestive problems and constipation for seven to eight months, affecting energy and mood
Two herniated discs at L4/L5/S1 with intermittent sciatica and back tightness triggered by sitting and by working hunched over
Roughly two hours of daily commuting on top of a 7-9 hour clinical day, arriving at the gym already exhausted
Eats out once or twice a day because cooking takes energy he does not have — 'it's just not fun anymore'
Has stopped doing his own hobbies because of how his body feels — 'I wanted to go play soccer today, but I'm just like, I'm going to be sore'
Bores of any fixed plan and drops it — 'I also get tired of doing the same plan'

objections.raw_quote: you have financial goals this year, I'm trying to move, I need to save money for a loan, to get a loan for an office, and I have goals for my dental office ... 6,000 just puts a pause on some of things that I wanted to achieve that are non-physical.
objections.rep_response: Isolated finances, ran the how-to-do-it reframe, opened the payment conversation and asked for a full financial picture; got cash on hand ($15,000) and the loan and moving commitments, then pushed toward credit and financing.

objections.raw_quote: I'm moving to New Jersey in August, September ... So I saved, I'm saving $8,000 for that. And so that $6,000 will take away from that. And so now I'll like $2,000 left for that. So financially, I'm not going to be able to do what I want to do within the next six months.
objections.rep_response: Minimised it — 'Okay, that would be like just slowing you a bit' — then argued that failing to invest in himself would delay the dental office more.

objections.raw_quote: I don't want to charge that much on a credit card if I don't have... The means to pay it all off in the same... I don't like going over my credit card limits ... I don't put the insurance on my credit cards. So I don't want to pay the insurance on my credit cards. I've never done that. never will, to be honest.
objections.rep_response: 'I respect that. However, we're talking about something important right now ... I understand you have some rules that you go by, but how do you feel? Maybe sometimes it's good to bend the rules for the better cause.' Proposed label: personal_financial_rule.

objections.raw_quote: can I think about it still and I don't want to just I have to sleep on it or like at least think another hour or two about it because I can't just commit right now
objections.rep_response: Asked 'Why not? Tell me, what's going through your head?', reframed it as numbers rather than desire, then booked a next-day call and took a $100 deposit.

objections.raw_quote: I wasn't expecting 6,000, to be honest, either.
objections.rep_response: Did not address the expectation gap; had already moved to structuring instalments.

tiers.note: The 12-month transformation was referenced as an option but no price was ever quoted for it on this call

offer.payment_plan_terms: Three routes were described: a third-party financing processor named as 'Piva', with terms unknown until an application is run; two instalments with no interest, half now and half in 30 days; or spreading over up to six months at $1,200 per month, which the rep said 'comes with a... Interest fee. Yeah, like the overall price is higher'. The $7,200 total implied by the six-month option was never stated.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Only on the deposit: 'If you say tomorrow to me, look, Andrew, I cannot pull it off. Okay. We'll give it back to you.'

prospect_financials.note: $15,000 in savings and checking, but committed: dental school loans being paid down, $8,000 earmarked for the August/September move, and an ongoing savings programme toward the $80,000-$100,000 a lender wants to see before granting a dental practice loan. Uses credit cards but never carries a balance and states he never will.

evidence: No programme purchase and no programme payment link; the only link sent and paid was a $100 refundable deposit

Explicit refusal to commit on the call: 'I can't just commit right now' and 'I would have to restructure some finances. I can't just be like, okay, I'm gonna just give you the 6,000 today. There's no way.'
Next-day call booked for 5:30pm Eastern, calendar invite confirmed received
Counter-evidence toward closed: he answered 'Yeah' to 'You're 100% sure you want to do this?', paid the deposit, and said of the price 'I think it's reasonable. I think it's fine'
Counter-evidence toward lost: he needs to speak to his CPA and a business partner, and the money is allocated against a practice-loan qualification threshold he cannot move
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call Monday 1 June at 5:30pm Eastern after he speaks to his CPA and reviews his numbers

notable.note: Excellent discovery and a genuinely skilled reframe from 'super shredded' to health and function, including talking the prospect down from a 10% body fat target on health grounds. Against that: a man with two herniated discs at L4/L5/S1 and intermittent sciatica was sold loaded kettlebell training with no question about clinical clearance, and a man in active treatment for depression had that depression used as a closing argument — 'if you will get back to depressive states or whatever, you won't perform on the level that you could be. So you won't be able to generate income.' The rep also pressed him to break a stated rule against carrying credit card debt, and quoted a six-month instalment plan of $1,200 a month without ever naming the $7,200 total.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion, worst between 00:47:00 and 01:02:00 where almost the entire money conversation is mis-attributed — the prospect's financial disclosures appear under the rep's label and the rep's questions under the prospect's. Roles were read from content. Also affected earlier: 'This back injury, when did it happen?' and 'How well actually do you know Trevor' sit correctly, but several answers around 00:11:41 to 00:12:35 are swapped mid-exchange. Numbers are internally inconsistent in one place: cash on hand is transcribed as 'I have like 15. 1,500. 15,000.' and read as $15,000 from the surrounding discussion of an $80,000-$100,000 savings target.
